question: Does TV distance maintain monotonic lambda-scaling of dynamical structure detection under realistic stochastic noise conditions (additive uniform, heteroscedastic state-dependent, mixed, and mean-preserving), or does noise destroy the metric's discriminating power before product-relevant noise levels are reached?
hypothesis: TV distance maintains monotonic lambda-scaling (Spearman rho(TV, lambda) >= 0.7 at each noise fraction) across all noise conditions up to 60% noise fraction, degrading gracefully rather than catastrophically. The noise fraction at which TV scaling breaks down (rho < 0.7) differs across noise types: mean-preserving noise breaks down earliest (least information loss), additive uniform noise breaks down latest (most information preserved), and heteroscedastic/mixed noise fall between.
falsifier: TV scaling fails (Spearman rho(TV, lambda) < 0.7 or p>0.05 after Bonferroni correction) at noise fraction <= 0.4 for ANY noise type, OR TV scaling degrades non-monotonically with noise fraction (Spearman rho between rho_TV and noise_fraction < 0.7), OR positive control fails (rules >90% at lambda=1, noise=0 for all 3 functions), OR null control fails (rules not significantly > memory at lambda=0, noise=0).
baselines: Action-conditioned rule baseline (majority vote of (state,action)->next_state) — same as parent
Pure nearest-neighbor memory baseline (no action conditioning) — same as parent
Variance-of-means baseline — same as parent, expected to degrade faster than TV under noise
Shuffle baseline (action labels permuted) — null for action-dependence
positive_control: At lambda=1, noise_fraction=0: rules achieve >90% test accuracy across all 3 quadratic function families. This replicates parent positive control and verifies pipeline integrity under the new DGP variants.
null_control: At lambda=0, noise_fraction=0: rules do not significantly outperform memory (paired t-test p>0.05). This replicates parent null control.
measurement_validity: Each noise-fraction x DGP-variant x function cell has 500 transitions for stable TV estimation
5 independent replications per cell (different RNG seeds) for variance estimation
Same 3 quadratic function families as parent (seeds 42, 43, 44) for direct comparability
Same state space (10 states) and action space (4 actions) as parent
Noise is injected AFTER deterministic signal, preserving signal structure
Frozen random seeds for reproducibility (base seed=42, replication seeds=1000..1004)
No target leakage: baselines fit on train only, TV computed on held-out transitions
Train/test split: 80/20 stratified by lambda and function within each noise condition
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) TV scaling monotonic degradation holds: Spearman rho(rho_TV_at_noise_fraction, noise_fraction) >= 0.7 across noise fractions for each noise type (Bonferroni corrected for 5 noise types x 3 functions = 15 comparisons), (2) TV scaling persists (rho >= 0.7) at noise_fraction <= 0.6 for ALL noise types, (3) positive control passes, (4) null control passes, (5) no pipeline errors: verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. If TV scaling breaks at noise_fraction <= 0.4 for any noise type, OR degrades non-monotonically, OR controls fail: verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING. If infrastructure prevents execution: MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: TV distance is robust to stochastic noise at levels typical of real Web transitions. Product pipeline can deploy TV-based regime detection with expected degradation quantified per noise type. The noise fraction at which TV breaks down provides a calibration bound for real-world confidence. Heteroscedastic robustness confirms TV works on pages with variable dynamic content.
product_consequence_negative: If TV scaling breaks at low noise fractions (<=0.4), the synthetic-to-real gap is likely insurmountable for raw TV distance. Product must either (a) develop noise-reduction preprocessing before TV computation, (b) use alternative metrics robust to stochastic transitions, or (c) restrict regime detection to low-noise Web transitions (e.g., static pages, deterministic APIs). This would substantially delay product deployment of physics-based regime detection.
estimated_cost: Low-moderate: pure synthetic data generation, offline computation. 5 DGP variants x 3 functions x 7 noise fractions x 500 transitions x 5 replications = 52,500 transitions total. TV computation is O(n^2) per cell but n=500 is small. Estimated runtime < 30 minutes on single machine.
expected_information_gain: High: This is the first test of TV distance robustness under realistic noise. The parent experiment validated TV on clean deterministic DGPs; this experiment bridges toward real Web conditions. Identifying which noise types break TV scaling first provides actionable guidance for product deployment (e.g., if mean-preserving noise is benign, many Web transitions may be regime-detectable despite stochasticity). If all noise types break TV at similar thresholds, the metric has a universal robustness bound.
